nodes.label: Expo animation build sequence
nodes.rationale: Nine ordered steps for React Native: the same gate and purpose questions as the web skill, then thread choice, properties, spring or timing, keeping work off the JS thread, press instead of hover, haptics, and reduced motion. Feel is judged only on a release build on the slowest supported device.

nodes.label: Two runtimes — RN runtime and UI runtime
nodes.rationale: Worklets make the split explicit: React renders on the RN runtime while worklets run every frame on the UI runtime. Motion that touches the RN runtime stutters as soon as the app does anything else, so the whole craft is keeping animation on the UI runtime. Mobile also has no hover, and the user's finger is on the element, which makes interruptibility and velocity handoff the baseline rather than polish.

nodes.label: Keep motion off the JS thread
nodes.source_location: 6. Keep it off the JS thread
nodes.rationale: Never setState from a gesture or scroll handler — one React render per frame is the biggest cause of jank in RN apps. scheduleOnRN (which replaces the deprecated runOnJS) belongs in onEnd or a threshold reaction, never in onUpdate. Shared values are read and written with .get()/.set() in worklets and handlers only, never during render, and worklet-called functions need the 'worklet' directive or they throw on device while working in the debugger.

nodes.label: Spring when a finger was involved
nodes.rationale: Springs carry velocity through an interruption while timing curves restart, so any gesture uses a spring expressed as duration plus dampingRatio rather than mass/stiffness/damping. Bounce is earned only when the gesture carried momentum. Press feedback is 100-150ms, small state changes 150-200ms, sheets a ~300ms spring, and screen transitions keep the platform default.

nodes.label: Press, not hover
nodes.rationale: Every hover affordance from the web has to be redesigned rather than ported. Feedback fires on press-in and commit on press-out, because waiting for the tap to complete feels dead. scale 0.97 over 100-150ms takes the label and icons with it, which is what reads as physical; touch targets stay 44x44pt with hitSlop rather than a grown visual.

nodes.label: Haptics rules
nodes.rationale: Three absolute rules: fire in the same frame as the visual at the causal moment, one per user action, and never as the only feedback since haptics are off system-wide for many users and silent on most Android hardware. Used sparingly they make an app feel expensive; used everywhere they get turned off.
